analyst_view.overall: Mid-table Celta (14th, 13 points, one win in five) host Villarreal (10th, 15 points) on Sunday evening, with both sides coming off European games: Villarreal play Slavia Prague in the Champions League on Wednesday and Celta host Bournemouth in the Europa League on Thursday, leaving Claudio Giraldez's side only three days to recover, and previews expect some rotation on both sides. Celta are without top striker Borja Iglesias (calf, out since mid-October, may return around now), Starfelt and Miguel Roman, plus Yoel Lago through a fifth yellow card (counted by the numbers). Villarreal lose Pau Navarro, sent off at Barcelona, and Saliba (ankle), while Gerard Moreno, Foyth and Ilias are working back from injury. No referee is named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals, already raised a little for the high-scoring past meetings and for Lago's absence in Celta's defence. Celta are still without their main striker Borja Iglesias and play on Thursday night, Villarreal miss Saliba in midfield, and the numbers do not know about these absences, so I lean slightly lower, about 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners, already lifting Celta for their 32 corners in six and Villarreal's habit of conceding them (39). Celta's wide play with Hugo Alvarez and Swedberg should keep that going, and rotation on both sides changes little. I stay at about 8.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards, already cut for Celta's quiet record (7 cards in six) and raised for past meetings. Villarreal have been booked more lately (15 in six, with Navarro sent off at Barcelona and Veiga on four yellows), but the numbers see that, and no referee is named yet. I stay at about 4.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.7 shots, already raising both sides for their recent volume (Celta +13%, Villarreal +8%). Tired legs after European games could cut the tempo, but two open, attacking sides who both concede plenty of shots keep it high, so the two balance out. I stay at about 26.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 shots on target, already lowering Villarreal for their poor recent accuracy (23 on target in six). Celta without Borja Iglesias lack their best finisher, but their 24 on target in the last six, mostly without him, is already in the numbers, and they face a Villarreal side that has allowed 37 in six. I stay at about 8.4.
